verdict.root_cause: At 21:14:07 UTC a platform-automation actor updated emailservice's image reference to an artifact tagged for a different service (quoteservice). From 21:15 onward emailservice is no longer the email application at all: it emits Apache startup output under pid 1, hits a fatal ports-configuration syntax error during config parse, exits, and is restarted on a ~60s cadence — a crash-restart loop in which the process never binds a listener. Because no instance ever becomes ready, the emailservice name stops resolving for callers: checkoutservice's outbound order-confirmation HTTP POST to the emailservice host on port 6060 fails at name lookup against the embedded Docker resolver (127.0.0.11:53) before any TCP connection, producing the single ERROR span in every failing checkout trace and the recurring warning per order. The failure is confined to the confirmation-notification branch — payment, shipping, cart-empty and the orders publish all still succeed — which is why checkoutservice's error ratio is partial (~8.3% peak) rather than total. emailservice's own error-ratio metric reads flat zero throughout, which is not health: a process that dies during config parse never serves a request it could fail, so it contributes no error-status calls. The running artifact is not the one that should be running; that, not any value in emailservice's own configuration, is the mechanism.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on emailservice. The change log (tr_a614468ba3ef) places exactly one change in the window — an image-reference update at 21:14:07 carrying a tag naming quoteservice, an automation actor, no config or scaling edits. The logs (tr_a6cd9169496c) show the consequence one minute later: healthy 200s at ~2ms up to 21:08, then from 21:15 a repeating ~60s cycle of Apache startup, config-variable warnings and a fatal ports syntax error under pid 1 — the wrong application refusing to start, not the email application misbehaving. The caller side (tr_ff3b2d09a3eb) names the failure precisely as DNS resolution of the emailservice hostname failing at the Docker resolver, i.e. no ready endpoint, and confirms the same code path succeeded at 21:08:05/21:08:09. Traces (tr_be48622726b0) show the only ERROR span in the failing path is checkoutservice's own outbound HTTP POST to the email endpoint, failing fast at ~2ms with no downstream service span in error. The emailservice zero-error metric (tr_626315519e37) is the classic misread flagged by cart-redis-misconfig and cart-bad-image-tag in the corpus: a component that never serves cannot emit errors, so flat zero is consistent with, not exculpatory of, total startup failure. Change queries on checkoutservice (tr_96a14b4ced79) and cartservice (tr_88e4683f49e2) are empty, removing the two obvious alternative rollback targets. The mechanism is a wrong artifact running, so the fix is to restore emailservice's correct image; a restart alone would only re-enter the crash loop, and there is no emailservice configuration value to revert — the ports file is the wrong artifact's own.
open_questions: The dominant customer-visible symptom is unexplained by this mechanism: checkoutservice PlaceOrder spans run 1.5s-29s with only tens of milliseconds attributable to child spans (tr_be48622726b0), and the erroring email POST itself lasts ~2ms. Whether this multi-second self-time is a side effect of resolver retries/backoff outside instrumentation, or a second concurrent fault, is not settled by any dispatch.

The change record lists the prior image reference as null (tr_a614468ba3ef), so the correct artifact to roll back to is not established by the evidence and must be recovered from the registry or deployment history.

Exact onset is unresolved. checkoutservice logs were truncated between 21:08:09 and 21:18:53 (tr_ff3b2d09a3eb), and the alert fired at 21:17:45 — roughly three minutes after the image change and two after the first crash-loop line. The gap is consistent with the causal chain but does not prove first-failure timing.

No latency percentile, CPU/memory/thread-pool or connection-pool saturation data was ever retrieved for checkoutservice (tr_50e819a89376), so a resource-side contribution to the latency cannot be excluded.

Change status for productcatalogservice, shippingservice, currencyservice, paymentservice and frauddetectionservice was never queried (tr_88e4683f49e2); four unmeasured edges from triage remain uninspected.
Whether the mis-targeted image was pushed to other services by the same automation run is unknown — only emailservice, cartservice and checkoutservice change logs were pulled.
